name: The Null Markets (Ghost Bazaar Circuit)
description: A rotating constellation of illegal pop-up bazaars coordinated through encrypted BCI pulses known as 'whisper-drops' — location data that dissolves from memory within 90 minutes of receipt. Unlike static underground markets, the Null Markets exist in a different abandoned structure every 72 hours: a decommissioned Solace Corp water reclamation plant in the Gray Zone-edge one night, a flooded parking cathedral in Tier 2's Pilsen Remnant district the next. Vendors include geneware surgeons, unlicensed augment installers, ghost-food collectives selling pre-corp seed varieties, and information brokers dealing in scrubbed corponation files. The market's unofficial curator — known only as Tessbreck — is believed to be an E.L.F. who has never physically occupied any single location.
cultural_impact: The Null Markets have normalized the idea of temporary commerce as a political act — buying from them is understood across the lower tiers as a deliberate refusal of corponation retail infrastructure. Dozens of above-ground Tier 2 businesses quietly source specialty goods through them, creating an invisible supply chain that runs beneath legitimate commerce.
key_figures: Constable Yevgenia Okoro-Brandt (enforcement officer who has never made an arrest there)
locations: Solace Corp Reclamation Plant 7 (decommissioned, the Gray Zone-edge)
The Drowned Lots (flooded pre-collapse parking structures, rotating)
story_hooks: A Tier 3 journalist receives a whisper-drop by mistake and arrives at a Null Market to find something that should not exist being sold openly — a synthetic child, listed as 'unclaimed property.'
Tessbreck sends an encoded message to a specific individual through a vendor's transaction receipt — someone who has never attended a Null Market and has no idea how they were found.

A corponation enforcement sweep finally locates a Null Market in progress, but the building is structurally compromised — the officers must decide whether to make arrests or help evacuate hundreds of the Gray Zone residents before the floor gives way.
